audit.whatIsWrong: Four rows print Jayce as the winner directly above prose explaining why Zaahen wins them: whys[1] "you can threaten to close the gap, punishing Jayce's poke attempts in your favour", whys[2] "Level 3 favours you", whys[5] "your bruiser stats survive his poke", whys[6] "an even Jayce can't duel your scaled bruiser body".
audit.why: Packet chart is Skill, Zaahen, Zaahen, Skill, Skill, Zaahen, Zaahen and the win rate is 52.9% over 1552 games. The mirror audit identified the identical inversion but deliberately did NOT fix it, on the stated belief that changing "Jayce" to "Zaahen" is a +20% length change the applier's band would reject. That belief is wrong: win[N] and phases[N].side are enum fields and are exempt from the length band, so the flip applies cleanly.
audit.corrected: Rows 1, 2, 5 and 6 flipped to Zaahen in both layers as matched pairs, with ratings raised to 6/10 and the four phase whys rewritten to state the real reason.

audit.whatIsWrong: Shock Blast is named as the tracked cooldown in twelve fields with no duration, and the page never mentions the stance-swap timer that governs everything Jayce does.
audit.why: Shock Blast is 16s at rank 1 (Jayce's Q has six ranks, 16/14/12/10/8/6). Thundering Blow is 20s at rank 1 and is his only escape from a committed all-in. The weapon swap is a flat 6s — that is the number that decides whether he can answer your gap-close at all, because swapping to Hammer to survive costs him his poke for the next six seconds. Grim Deliverance is 110/95/80.
audit.corrected: The 16s, 20s, 6s and 110s written into the phases, spikes, mid and breakdown.cooldowns.

audit.whatIsWrong: (a) spikes[0] writes "Ranged Q (To the Skies / Shock Blast)" — To the Skies! is the Hammer-stance leap, a melee gap-closer; the ranged poke is Shock Blast in Cannon stance. Presenting them as one ranged ability is a stance error, not just a naming one. (b) The packet's flag on "To the Skies" is also genuine — the name carries an exclamation mark. (c) "Final Retribution" (Grim Deliverance) and "Golden Onslaught" (Aureate Rush) again. (d) The weapon swap is an auto-attack reset and its first Cannon attack shreds armour and MR — absent entirely.
audit.why: missingInteractions flags the swap reset: the wind-up on the stance change is the tell, not the cast. It matters doubly here because the first attack after swapping to Cannon reduces your resistances, so the swap is both his burst opener and the reason your armour reads lower than you expect in that trade.
audit.corrected: Stances separated correctly, To the Skies! spelled with its mark, Zaahen's real names used, and the swap's 6s named as the cost of him escaping into melee.

notes: The mirror left this chart broken on a false premise, and it is worth flagging beyond this matchup: its note says flipping 'Jayce' to 'Zaahen' is a +20% length change that the applier would reject. win[N] and phases[N].side are enum fields, exempt from the band, so the flip applies cleanly — I have proposed all four rows as matched pairs. If the same reasoning was applied elsewhere in that agent's slice, those charts are still inverted too. Stance error worth noting: spikes[0] presented 'To the Skies! / Shock Blast' as one ranged ability. To the Skies! is the Hammer-stance leap; a player waiting to dodge a ranged 'To the Skies!' is watching for something that does not exist.
